newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia threatens to withdraw Georgia peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: Russia threatens to withdraw Georgia peacekeepers.

text.p: A senior foreign ministry official said on Wednesday Russia would withdraw its peacekeeping troops from a buffer zone between Georgia and the breakaway province of Abkhazia unless Georgia formally extended their mandate.

"If by July 31 we do not get confirmation from Georgia that it agrees to prolong the mandate we will withdraw the peacekeepers," Gennady Ilychev told Reuters. "That is the official position of the foreign ministry."

The mandate of the 1,500 peacekeepers expires on Thursday. Ilychev, who is the foreign ministry's special envoy on the Georgian-Abkhazian talks, said Russia needed both Abkhazia and Georgia to agree to keep the troops in the buffer zone.

"The Abkhaz side has noted the key role of the peacekeepers ...in securing peace there. But the main condition is that both sides agree -- and we still have nothing from Georgia," he said. "After July 31 there will be no reason to keep the troops in the zone."
Some 10,000 people were killed in a 1992-93 separatist war between Abkhazia and the Tbilisi government, and at least 150,000 ethnic Georgian refugees have not yet been able to return to the province.

Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze, who has repeatedly said the peacekeepers would have to widen their remit to help refugees return or leave, on Monday changed his stance and urged caution. He said Western leaders had cautioned him against forcing the Russians out.
